source_review.notes: Reviewed author/official or university-hosted Chord, Kademlia, Pastry, CAN, Dynamo, corrected-Chord, and libp2p Kademlia sources. All seven final chapter destinations returned HTTP 200; the initially selected Cornell CAN URL returned 404 and was replaced before review. Routing, convergence, and security claims remain scoped to their stated metric, topology, timing, and adversary assumptions.

evidence: Checked identifier width, successor, fingers, successor lists, XOR distance, k-buckets, alpha, records, churn, stabilization, Sybil, and eclipse terminology.
Checked circular, XOR, prefix, and geometric metrics are kept separate.
Checked routing ownership, record placement, successful replication, and record truth are distinct contracts.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Interval equality, wrap, identity/endpoint binding, and record freshness are explicit.

evidence: Recomputed node 1 fingers [4,4,8,12] on the four-bit fixture.
Recomputed owner of key 10 as 12 and route [1,8,12].
Exhaustively recomputed all 64 start/key routes and their successor owners.
Recomputed the post-join nodes, owner 10, route [1,8,10], Exercise 1 fingers, owners, and wrap route.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All identifiers are unsigned integers modulo the stated space.

evidence: Derived successor-fallback termination from a correct finite live successor cycle.
Derived closest-preceding-finger progress from strict modular interval membership.
Reviewed Kademlia XOR ordering, candidate-set progress, and termination conditions.
Separated ideal logarithmic results from stabilization, record, and Byzantine properties.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The logarithmic Chord statement retains uniform-ID and sufficiently correct-table assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed zero, maximum, exact node IDs, wrap, singleton, duplicate IDs, wrong metrics, and broken successor cycles.
Reviewed stale/dead contacts, timeouts, parallelism, cancellation, duplicates, late responses, churn, partitions, NAT, relays, and restart.
Reviewed invalid/expired/conflicting records, failed replica writes, repair, mutable versions, and provider endpoint validation.
Reviewed malicious bootstrap, Sybil/eclipse/poisoning, amplification, oversized responses, spam, quotas, and correlated failures.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model excludes asynchronous messages, failures, stabilization, records, transport, persistence, and adversaries.

evidence: Verified every forwarding step is a strict clockwise advance or justified immediate successor termination.
Verified no fixture route repeats a forwarding node and every route ends at the linear successor oracle.
Verified join snapshot recomputation changes the key-10 owner and route consistently.
Verified exact twelve-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the safe verifier.
invariant_checking.notes: Final wrap to the starting node can be correct ownership and is distinguished from a forwarding loop.

evidence: Reviewed Chord progress against the correct-successor-cycle premise.
Reviewed XOR lookup progress against validated candidate ordering and bounded iterative state.
Reviewed record correctness as a separate validation/reconciliation proof obligation.
Reviewed join/repair safety against retained old copies and acknowledged new replicas.
proof_review.notes: No asynchronous stabilization, Byzantine routing, replica-consistency, or Internet-liveness proof is claimed.

evidence: Separated Chord, Kademlia, Pastry, CAN, centralized, gossip, and federated designs.
Separated overlay hops from network latency and desired placement from acknowledged durability.
The model explicitly disclaims stabilization and distributed-network evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Stable honest routing results are not generalized to churn, open membership, or adversarial peers.

evidence: The bisect-based model passed exact expected output under the safe verifier.
An independent implementation reproduced all fixture routes and post-join results.
All seven final reference destinations returned HTTP 200.
Structure, links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippets passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No protocol implementation, asynchronous simulator/model checker, cross-version wire run, churn/partition/NAT/Sybil campaign, benchmark, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives structured overlay routing while separating geometry, stabilization, record semantics, replication, membership, transport, and threat controls.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed bootstrap, identity/endpoints, maintenance, record validation/expiry, replicas/repair, bounded RPC/storage, persistence/revalidation, observability, and incident controls.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review fixes the abstraction boundaries; one exhaustive small Chord model anchors routing; ten examples cover metrics, records, failures, and attacks; five exercises span derivation, Kademlia state, protocol design, and evaluation.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official/university-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external Chord, Kademlia, Pastry, CAN, Dynamo, libp2p, networking, distributed-systems, database, cryptographic, security, SRE, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither asynchronous stabilization, churn tolerance, Byzantine/Sybil/eclipse resistance, record/replica consistency, durable storage, Internet/NAT operation, protocol interoperability, certification, nor deployment fitness.
